title: Newcomers Cobb and Joe Wilder isolated in Hampton's band
summary: Wilder and Cobb joined together in San Francisco, roomed together, were left out by the band's cliques, and Wilder won respect by sight-reading a hard chart.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Hear what I'm saying to you. I'm tell -- see, Joe Wilder and I joined the band at the same time in San Francisco, Hamp's band. And they isolated us, and we were roommates on the road, two newest guys in the band. Joe took Carl George's place. And I took Illinois' place, and the syndicate was for Illinois and Carl George because that was the Joe Newman was with this.

And give you a strange thing about Joe Newman, they all looking at Joe and, you know, they don't know. We were on our way back, going towards East, going towards Chicago, and we got into Denver. We played Denver a night. Joe had been there a long time and going to have some fun. So he told -- he said to Hamp, said, why don't you call 102, signifying. 102 was Trumpet Reveille that Milton Buckner did with 64ths in it and everything.

So Joe looked at Curly. Hamp said, ch-ch-ch-ch-- (inaudible) we're going to have to rehearse. And Joe looked and said, you could knock it off. That's how trained he was. Playing -- he played it verbatim. He looked at it, and from that point on they all respected Joe. You couldn't get Joe Newman off of Wilder. He was asking questions, and before everything was significant, like, you know, (inaudible). But he showed them something.
How long does this go on for a newcomer in the band?
I don't know, but they would leave us, and they would say (inaudible). They knew where they were going. We were new in the band. We had to feel our way. But we stuck together.
Well, did that happen in any other band?

I don't know. I never had that experience with anybody because this is the first big band because I told you our band, Milton (inaudible) band was a family band. And this is one thing I feel, but with Joe being with me, with Joe Wilder being with me, we -- we've -- we handled it pretty well, and they get their cabs and leave us, don't tell us where they're going, where to stop or nothing. And that's how isolated they were, and they syndicated different things.
It's a good thing you weren't alone.
Well, I had Joe with me, and we finally found our way. And I tell you one thing. Today I know my way around anywhere I go.
And I made friends. Yeah, well, I mean you were both able to take care of yourself musically, so there was that,
